name: Jersey
summary: Crown Dependency outside the UK and EU. No capital gains tax, no inheritance or gift tax, no wealth tax. Income including dividends is taxed at a flat 20%. Probate stamp duty up to 0.75%, capped at £100,000. Wealthy newcomers normally come as High Value Residents: minimum £250,000 tax a year, 1% on income above £1.25m.

regimes.name: Ordinary Jersey residence
regimes.description: Residents pay a flat 20% income tax on worldwide income. No capital gains, inheritance, gift or wealth tax; probate stamp duty of up to 0.75% (capped at £100,000).
regimes.eligibility: Tax residence in Jersey. Buying or renting property needs housing status (Control of Housing and Work); newcomers without it have very limited housing options, which is why wealthy arrivals use the HVR route.

capital_gains.summary: Jersey has no capital gains tax. Gains by a resident private investor on securities, a private business or real estate are not taxed, unless the activity is a trade (taxed as income at 20%). Stamp duty or land transaction tax applies on buying Jersey property.

capital_gains.rate_basis: No capital gains tax in Jersey; income tax (20%) applies to income, and to trading profits, not to capital gains.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Share or property dealing that amounts to a trade is taxed as income at 20%; Jersey property development profits are taxed at 20%.
open_questions: PwC 'other taxes' page does not expressly state 'no CGT'; widely documented but not quoted from an official Revenue Jersey page in this research.

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed as income at a flat 20% (the alternative marginal calculation at 26% only helps low incomes). For 2026 the income tax exemption threshold is £21,250; all married couples are taxed independently from 2026. High Value Residents pay 1% on non-Jersey-property income above £1.25m (see special regime).

dividends.rate_basis: Flat 20% standard rate on net income after allowances (PwC). Foreign dividend withholding is relieved by a double tax credit only where Jersey has a double taxation agreement covering that income; otherwise the taxpayer may ask for the income to be taxed net of the foreign tax (Revenue Jersey). Jersey has no treaty with the United States and few others, so the foreign tax is modelled as a deduction: 20% x (dividend - 15% withholding). Most Jersey companies pay 0% corporate tax, so no imputation credit arises on typical domestic dividends.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Exemption threshold £21,250 (2026); relevant only at low income.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No withholding tax on dividends, interest or royalties paid by Jersey companies to non-residents (PwC).
dividends.treaty_network: Small set of double tax agreements (UK, Guernsey, Isle of Man and a few others); no US income tax treaty, so US dividends suffer 30% US withholding. Where there is no agreement covering the income, foreign tax is relieved only by taxing the income net of that tax (Revenue Jersey); where there is one, by credit (Income Tax (Jersey) Law 1961, Art. 111-112).
open_questions: Exact treaty count not verified from an official list. Partner countries with a Jersey treaty covering dividends would give a credit instead of a deduction; the model treats all foreign dividends as from non-treaty countries.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Modelled as the 'holding_company' structure regime: a Jersey company pays 0% on investment income and gains; the resident shareholder pays 20% on distributions (Schedule DIX, up to their share of profits taxed below 20%).

wealth_tax.summary: No wealth tax or net worth tax.

sources.title: Jersey - Individual - Other taxes

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Parish rates are levied on property by each parish (modest). Stamp duty applies to purchases of Jersey real estate; non-main-residence purchases carry an extra 4 percentage points since 2023.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance tax and no gift tax. A probate stamp duty applies to the personal (movable) estate: 0.5% up to £100,000, then £500 plus £75 per £10,000 (0.75%), capped at £100,000 for estates above £13.36m. For a Jersey-domiciled person it applies to worldwide movable estate.

inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax. Stamp duty applies to gifts of Jersey immovable property (land) as for transfers.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Probate duty (Stamp Duties and Fees (Jersey) Law 1998, Schedule 3, item 9, consolidated version in force 1 January 2026): no fee up to GBP 10,000 net; GBP 50 for each GBP 10,000 (or part) up to GBP 100,000; GBP 500 on the first GBP 100,000 plus GBP 75 for each additional GBP 10,000 (or part) up to GBP 13,360,000; flat GBP 100,000 above. Item 9(2) adds a fixed GBP 107 (professional application) or GBP 268 (other). other_transfer_cost_rate 0.0075 is the marginal rate up to the cap; for a GBP 30m movable estate the effective cost is about 0.33%. Not indexed: the amounts change only by amending Regulations.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Lifetime gifts of shares and portfolios attract no duty, so the probate duty can be avoided by lifetime transfers or holding structures. Jersey succession law gives spouse and children rights over part of movable estate (not a tax; not verified here).
inheritance.foreign_assets: Probate duty covers worldwide personal estate of a Jersey-domiciled deceased; only Jersey-situs estate for others (Art. 5).
inheritance.domicile_rules: Duty base depends on Jersey domicile at death. No tax tail. Families arriving from the UK remain within UK IHT under the residence-based test from 6 April 2025 for up to 10 years after leaving, depending on years of UK residence.
open_questions: Whether Jersey still has légitime (forced heirship) rights over movables was not verified.

regimes.name: High Value Residency (2(1)(e) housing consent)
regimes.description: Discretionary residency for wealthy newcomers. Jersey property income is taxed at 20%; other income at 20% on the first £1.25m and 1% above. New HVRs (applications from 14 July 2023) must pay at least £250,000 a year: with income under £1.25m they are deemed to have enough income to pay that minimum.
regimes.eligibility: Application to the Government of Jersey (via Locate Jersey); granted at discretion considering economic and social benefit and financial history. Government stated in 2023 an expectation of net worth of at least £10m excluding the main home and a minimum property purchase of £3.5m (houses) / £1.75m (apartments), confirmation of final figures pending. Consent gives the right to buy or rent property.

lump_sum.notes: Minimum annual tax of £250,000 per applicant (gov.je). Covers income up to £1.25m; income above £1.25m (except Jersey property income at 20%) is taxed at 1%. Spouses are taxed independently. HVRs approved before 14 July 2023 stay on older terms (£170,000 minimum under the 2018 rules).

dividends.summary: For an HVR, dividends above the first £1.25m of income are taxed at 1%; the first £1.25m is taxed at 20%, subject to a minimum total tax of £250,000.

dividends.rate_basis: Marginal rate 1% on non-Jersey-property income above £1.25m; the £250,000 minimum is modelled as the lump sum. Foreign tax relief as in the standard regime (deduction where no treaty applies).
dividends.withholding_outbound: No withholding tax on dividends paid by Jersey companies to non-residents.
dividends.treaty_network: As standard regime (foreign tax relieved by a credit under a treaty, otherwise by taxing the income net of it).

regimes.duration_note: No time limit: the HVR tax treatment applies for as long as the individual holds 2(1)(e) housing consent, stays Jersey resident and meets the conditions of approval (including the minimum tax); if a condition is breached, the treatment reverts to ordinary rules from that year onwards (Revenue Jersey HVR guidance).

regimes.name: Jersey investment holding company (0% company)
regimes.description: The family funds a Jersey company that holds the listed portfolio. Jersey companies pay 0% income tax on investment income, and there is no capital gains tax, so the company pays nothing on dividends or gains. The shareholders are taxed at 20% only when value is taken out of the company (dividend, buy-back, liquidation); profits it keeps are not taxed on them, because the deemed distribution rules were repealed for profits accruing from 1 January 2012. Foreign withholding tax on the company's dividends is a final cost.
regimes.eligibility: Any Jersey resident can incorporate a company under the Companies (Jersey) Law 1991; a Jersey-incorporated company is resident in Jersey (Income Tax (Jersey) Law 1961, Art. 123(1)(a)). It must be a passive investment holder: financial services, utility, Jersey property and large retail activities are taxed at 10% or 20%. US citizens are excluded (CFC/PFIC rules).
regimes.duration_note: Ordinary company rules with no time limit; the company lasts as long as the family keeps it.

capital_gains.summary: Jersey has no capital gains tax, and a company pays income tax at a general rate of 0% (PwC), so gains realised by the holding company are not taxed.
capital_gains.rate_basis: General corporate rate 0% (PwC); Jersey has no capital gains tax. Rates 0 for listed securities and private business sale; real estate outside the island likewise 0.
capital_gains.professional_trader: A company trading in securities is taxed on trading profits at the same 0% general rate; only the higher-rate activities listed by the revenue authority differ.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign gains are treated the same way.

open_questions: Real estate in the island is taxed at 20% in a company; the family portfolio is listed securities, so the figure here is for those.

dividends.summary: Dividends received by a Jersey company are income taxed at the general 0% corporate rate. Foreign withholding tax suffered is not recoverable.
dividends.rate_basis: General corporate rate 0% (PwC Jersey corporate): a company that is not a financial services, utility, Jersey property or large retail business pays no income tax. Foreign withholding tax is lost.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No withholding tax on dividends paid by Jersey companies to non-residents (PwC).
dividends.treaty_network: As the standard regime; at a 0% rate any foreign withholding on the company's dividends cannot be credited and is a final cost.
dividends.holding_company_notes: This regime models the company itself.

structure.entity: Private company limited by shares (Companies (Jersey) Law 1991), investment holding
structure.payout_notes: A distribution (cash dividend, buy-back, redemption, liquidation payment, repayment of a member's loan, benefit in kind; Income Tax (Jersey) Law 1961, Art. 3AE) to a Jersey-resident individual is taxed under Schedule DIX at 20% up to the individual's allocated share of 'specified profits' (profits taxed at less than 20%), and in full under the 'simplified basis' (Comptroller's guide, s.3.1 and 4). Anything above that share is taxed under Schedule DIII and can be exempt (capital profits, return of share capital, repayment of loan principal; Art. 78(1A)), so 20% is the ceiling on payout tax. Profits kept in the company are not taxed on the shareholder (deemed distributions repealed from 1 January 2012). High Value Residents pay 1% on income above GBP 1.25m, which could lower the payout tax; this regime assumes ordinary residence.
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: A Jersey-incorporated company is resident in Jersey unless centrally managed and controlled in a country taxing companies at 20% or more (Art. 123(1)(a)). Distribution rules (Art. 3AE) catch value taken out in other forms, and the Comptroller will monitor the use of trusts (Art. 134A). The Companies (Jersey) Law 1991 and the registered-office and beneficial-ownership requirements apply; their cost is not sourced here.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: A liquidation payment is a distribution (Art. 3AE(1)(b)), taxed at 20% up to the shareholder's share of specified profits, the rest under Schedule DIII (capital profits and returned capital are exempt). Jersey has no exit tax on individuals; no dividend withholding is levied on payments to non-residents.

These are qualified-tenant (local market) homes; HVRs with 2(1)(e) consent can rent any property. Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.

P.51/2026: the States Assembly site (statesassembly.je) blocks automated access, so its text could not be read. The only mention found is a commercial guide (Global Law Experts) saying it 'sharpened the minimum tax and housing expectations', with no figures. A separate proposition, P.19/2026 (Deputy Renouf), to cap the number of 2(1)(e) grants was scheduled for debate on 25 February 2026 and opposed by the Council of Ministers; its outcome was not verified. Revenue Jersey's HVR guidance (checked 2026-10-15) shows no 2026 change except independent taxation of spouses. HVR terms are recorded as on gov.je.

Spouses and the High Value Resident minimum: Revenue Jersey says the GBP 250,000 minimum is 'on the applicant's own taxable income' and that independent taxation applies to HVRs from 2026, but does not say whether a spouse who holds part of the portfolio is a second applicant with a second minimum. The recipe assumes the consent holder owns the portfolio.

Needs an engine change: High Value Residents pay 20% on the first GBP 1.25m of other income and 1% above, with a GBP 250,000 floor. The model charges a fixed GBP 250,000, which is right up to GBP 1.25m of income and understates tax by 1% of income above it (e.g. GBP 2m of income: GBP 257,500).
